questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Quality of education and being somewhere in Latin America

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Universidade de São Paulo is a great university with a lovely campus and very high quality of education. The faculty of FFLCH also did a great job of making the process of going on exchange easy, moreover they arranged a group of students to do a bunch of social activities together with the rest of the exchange students, which was an amazing opportunity to meet new people. 
Unfortunately there was a student strike while I was there which lasted about 1,5 months, which naturally limited my time studying at the university. Otherwise amazing experience.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy enough if you looked for it.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: My faculty FFLCH provided all information necessary. They also helped with filling out documentation for foreigners at the police.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very easy, just look in facebook groups for housing near Butantã. Find a location as close to uni as possible, but stay away from any places near P3, as it is less safe in that area.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: STAY AS CLOSE TO THE UNIVERSITY AS POSSIBLE. Traffic in São Paulo is no joke.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: You have to find housing yourself and no help is provided. It's easy enough to find housing in facebook groups, and rent is not too bad from an european perspective. You do have to look through a lot of options as many of them are pretty bad and depressing. I was very happy with the room I found.

Additional comments:

questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Very high quality of education.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The courses I took had a strong marxist discourse, which was refreshing. Especially relevant in a brazilian context

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Geografia do Turismo
Biogeografia
Regionalização do Espaço Brasileiro

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Regionalização do Espaço Brasileiro gives a good foundation of how Brazil was founded and the inequality through the country. 
Geografia do Turismo is a strong criticism of tourism and all that follows. A lot more interesting than you might think at first. The professor in both courses is amazing and speaks slow and very clear.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
Food can be really inexpensive if you eat at university, as it costs only 2R$ (3kr/0,5€) per meal. Eating out is also pretty cheap. Cooking yourself is not cheap though as prices in supermarkets are compareable to europe.
You'll also end up taking ubers a lot, as it is the safest option to get home at night. Luckily it's pretty cheap.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food at uni! So cheap and filling. Public transport it also pretty cheap. Get a bilhete unico! You can get them at most bus terminals.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Plenty of sport opportunities, they have a cinema (cineusp) that show movies each day, and great parties at uni every weekend

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Written above

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Cineusp and join a sports team. There's also a lot of people drumming at campus

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to museums. There are many great. And go to the beach! It's closer than you think for a weekend trip.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Brazilians are very welcoming. You will be lost without speaking portuguese as english isn't spoken.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to parties

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Taking care on the streets.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Brazilian culture is amazing. Great people, food and especially music

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Learn portuguese (classes are offered at USP)
2. Don't take too challeging courses, you'll want to enjoy life there
3. Live close to USP, but not by P3
